interest: Reveals interwar diplomacy regarding Japanese tax laws, treaty rights, and using foreign tax credits to prevent diplomatic conflicts.
overview: This file compiles State Department despatches, legal memoranda, and diplomatic correspondence from 1931 to 1937 concerning Japanese income and corporate taxation affecting American interests. It documents assessments of whether Japanese tax laws violated the 1911 commercial treaty regarding American insurance firms, corporate branches, perpetual leases in Yokohama, consular staff, and missionaries, detailing why U.S. officials avoided formal protests.
